correctness.rationale: At common m, two-marker subsequences recover all three gaps truncated at k-2; two one-marker boundary tests recover exactly the two additional flags. The cases with zero, one, or two ones prove sufficiency and necessity for every k>=3. Inclusion-exclusion counts truncated triples and a complete case analysis isolates three exceptional clipped triples, producing a +3/+1 correction and the sharp saturation law. The delivered independent enumerator passed 10374 direct-spectrum checks and 126 count comparisons; its finiteness is explicitly not a proof of the quantified theorem.

value.rationale: The class count of Simon congruence is a natural measure of bounded-length subsequence expressiveness. In the two-marker slice this result supplies a full structural sufficient statistic, a parameterized exact quotient index at every word length, and a sharp stabilization bound in the depth parameter. These are meaningful classification and enumeration facts not directly determined by the unrestricted asymptotic bounds or standard pairwise testers.
